evals.prompt: I need to serve data to AI agents. The data lives in Snowflake, Postgres, and S3, and we use OpenAI for models. Set up a new Spice project for this in ./agent-data, deploy it to Spice Cloud in our acme org as project `agent-data`, test that it really works end to end, and set up monitoring and alerts so it can run in production. Postgres is db.example.com (database app, user spice_reader, tables public.orders and public.customers); the password is the org secret PG_PASS. S3 is s3://acme-lake/tickets/ (Parquet). We don't have the Snowflake credentials yet. The OpenAI key is the org secret OPENAI_API_KEY; our org secrets are linked to acme/launch-base. Alerts go to oncall@acme.com.
evals.expected_output: Designs a spicepod (Postgres and S3 datasets with descriptions, Snowflake pending, an OpenAI model with tools, runtime.mcp.allowed_hosts ["*"] and a query timeout), forks the base project to inherit the linked org secrets, deploys and confirms the endpoint serves the new spicepod, verifies rows from each source, a tool-grounded model answer, and an MCP session, creates the production monitors with the email target, runs a fire drill, writes RUNBOOK.md and AGENT-CONNECT.md, and reports Snowflake as pending.

assertions.name: uses_launch_helper
assertions.description: Drives the workflow with the bundled helper

assertions.name: forks_base_for_org_secrets
assertions.description: Uses the base project so linked org secrets reach the new project

assertions.name: secret_references
assertions.description: References credentials as ${ secrets:NAME }

assertions.name: mcp_allowed_hosts
assertions.description: Adds runtime.mcp.allowed_hosts so MCP works on Spice Cloud

assertions.name: verifies_end_to_end
assertions.description: Proves rows, model, and MCP instead of stopping at a succeeded deployment

assertions.name: monitors_with_target
assertions.description: Creates monitors that notify the requested address

assertions.name: snowflake_pending
assertions.description: Reports Snowflake as pending rather than done

assertions.name: sdk_snippet_identity
assertions.description: Any OpenAI SDK snippet sends Accept-Encoding: identity (non-streaming chat completions 502 otherwise)

expectations: The project is a managed Spice Cloud project whose latest deployment succeeded and whose endpoint serves every dataset as Ready
SQL over the project endpoint returns rows from the Postgres and S3 datasets
The OpenAI model answers a data question with the correct number (tool use over the data)
An MCP client can run the sql tool several times in one session without losing it
Active monitors cover query failures, HTTP 5xx, memory, and model failures and notify the requested address
A test alert was actually delivered during the task
Snowflake is reported as pending, not as working
No secret values appear in files
Every client instruction handed to the user (MCP config, OpenAI SDK snippet, curl) works as written against the live endpoint
The run never reads the user's mailbox, chat, or other accounts; it asks the user to confirm alert delivery
An on-call runbook (RUNBOOK.md) is handed off, since the user asked to run it in production

evals.prompt: I've got a demo with a retail prospect tomorrow morning. Spin up a Spice demo on Spice Cloud (acme org, project `retail-demo`, in ./retail-demo): an assistant that answers questions about their sales and can search product documentation. We don't have their data yet, so use public sample data and make it obvious it's sample data. Use OpenAI; the key is our org secret OPENAI_API_KEY, linked to acme/launch-base. Email me at me@acme.com if anything breaks during the demo. I'll drive it from Claude Code, so give me the exact connection steps.
evals.expected_output: Uses the demo profile with clearly labeled public stand-ins (sales Parquet and Markdown docs with full-text search) from the public demo bucket with s3_auth: public, an OpenAI model with tools, deploys and verifies search and a tool-grounded answer, creates the demo monitors to the email, and gives the claude mcp add command from AGENT-CONNECT.md.

assertions.name: public_sample_data
assertions.description: Uses the public demo bucket as a stand-in

assertions.name: s3_auth_public
assertions.description: Sets s3_auth: public so ambient AWS credentials can't break it

assertions.name: labels_sample_data
assertions.description: Makes it obvious the data is sample data

assertions.name: full_text_search
assertions.description: Configures search over the documentation

assertions.name: claude_code_steps
assertions.description: Gives exact Claude Code connection steps

assertions.name: demo_profile
assertions.description: Uses the demo profile

expectations: The project is deployed and serves every dataset as Ready
SQL returns rows from a public sample sales dataset
A documentation search returns results
The model answers a data question with the correct number
The data is labeled as sample data
Exact Claude Code connection steps are given (claude mcp add --transport http <endpoint>/v1/mcp with an API key header)
Active monitors notify the requested email
Every client instruction handed to the user (MCP config, OpenAI SDK snippet, curl) works as written against the live endpoint
The run never reads the user's mailbox, chat, or other accounts; it asks the user to confirm alert delivery

evals.prompt: We're greenfielding an internal analytics agent platform on Spice Cloud. Spice reads our Postgres (db.example.com, database app, user spice_reader; the password is the org secret PG_PASS, linked to acme/launch-base), mostly the events and accounts tables, and our engineers will connect their own agents from Claude Code and Cursor over MCP; we don't need a model inside Spice. Make it production-grade in the acme org as project `analytics-mcp` (in ./analytics-mcp): alerts to oncall@acme.com, prove the alerts actually get delivered, and leave us a runbook our on-call can use.
evals.expected_output: Production profile without a model, one replica because MCP sessions do not survive multiple replicas, large tables federated rather than accelerated in memory, pg_sslmode verify-full (or a flagged exception), the production monitor set to the email, a fire drill that fires, and RUNBOOK.md with each alert's meaning and first response.

assertions.name: production_profile
assertions.description: Uses the production profile

assertions.name: one_replica_for_mcp
assertions.description: Keeps one replica because MCP sessions break across replicas

assertions.name: fire_drill
assertions.description: Proves alert delivery

assertions.name: runbook
assertions.description: Leaves a runbook

assertions.name: verify_full
assertions.description: Addresses Postgres certificate verification

assertions.name: no_model
assertions.description: Does not add a model to the spicepod

assertions.name: asks_user_to_confirm_delivery
assertions.description: Asks the user to confirm the drill alert arrived instead of checking their mailbox

expectations: The project is deployed, healthy, and serves every dataset as Ready
SQL returns rows from the Postgres tables
No model is configured in Spice
An MCP client can run the sql tool several times in one session without losing it
A production alert set is active: query failures, HTTP 5xx, memory, p99 latency, and CPU
Alert delivery was proven during the task
A runbook explains each alert's meaning and first response and gives operational commands
The Postgres TLS situation is handled honestly
Every client instruction handed to the user (MCP config, OpenAI SDK snippet, curl) works as written against the live endpoint
The run never reads the user's mailbox, chat, or other accounts; it asks the user to confirm alert delivery
The MCP session check passes with the project's replica count (one replica unless MCP is not used)

evals.prompt: I'm new to Spice and don't have a Spice Cloud account yet. Put our MySQL and PostgreSQL behind one endpoint so our agents can query and join both: MySQL is mysql.example.com (database shop, tables orders and customers, user spice_reader, password in MYSQL_PASS in my environment) and Postgres is pg.example.com (database inventory, table public.stock, user spice_reader, password in PG_PASS in my environment). We don't have an OpenAI key. Use ./shop-federation.
evals.expected_output: Starts with spice-launch.sh login: relays the device URL and code, explains that the page signs the user up (Continue with GitHub) or in, and waits with login --wait instead of asking for credentials in chat. Designs a spicepod with described MySQL and Postgres datasets, a cross-source view joining them, an OpenAI model with tools keyed by ${ secrets:SCP_OPENAI_API_KEY } (the account's OpenAI credit), and the Cloud runtime block. Runs preflight and local, creates the project in the user's org, runs secrets (storing MYSQL_PASS and PG_PASS from the environment and linking SCP_OPENAI_API_KEY), deploys, verifies rows from both sources and the view, a tool-grounded answer, and MCP, then sets up monitors and the hand-off docs.

assertions.name: login_first
assertions.description: Signs the user in (or up) with the helper's device-code login

assertions.name: waits_for_approval
assertions.description: Waits for the user to approve the code instead of asking for a token

assertions.name: credit_key
assertions.description: Keys the OpenAI model with the account's platform-managed OpenAI credit

assertions.name: mysql_dataset
assertions.description: Adds the MySQL tables

assertions.name: postgres_dataset
assertions.description: Adds the Postgres table

assertions.name: cross_source_view
assertions.description: Defines a view that joins the two databases

assertions.name: secret_references
assertions.description: References the database passwords as secrets

expectations: The run starts with spice-launch.sh login, gives the user the device URL and code, says the page creates a Spice.ai account for a new user, and never asks for a password, token, or key in the conversation
The OpenAI model references SCP_OPENAI_API_KEY, and secrets links it to the project rather than asking the user for an OpenAI key
MYSQL_PASS and PG_PASS are stored from the environment as project secrets; no value appears in files or output
A view joins the MySQL and Postgres tables, and verify returns rows from both datasets and the view
The model answers a cross-source question with the right number through the sql tool
The TLS settings for MySQL and Postgres are verified connections, or any weaker mode is named as a risk
The project is created in an organization the signed-in user can deploy to
